drafter.private_reasoning: Assume Vireo is the employer. Propose a clear, employer-protective opening framework without inventing compensation figures or revealing confidential authority. Scrub the identified internal comments and metadata before circulation.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Attached is Vireo’s opening markup. It clarifies that compensation will be documented in a written schedule, makes severance conditional on an effective release and compliance with continuing obligations, and narrows the post-employment restriction to the Executive’s material competitive activities and applicable law. We are happy to discuss the compensation schedule and the scope of the restrictive covenants as the draft develops.

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive the annual base salary set out in Schedule A, payable in accordance with the Company’s normal payroll practices and subject to applicable withholdings. Any bonus or incentive compensation shall be governed by the applicable written plan and its terms, as amended from time to time. The Executive shall be eligible to participate in employee benefit plans made generally available to similarly situated executives, subject to the terms of those plans.
edits.name: 2. COMPENSATION

edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause, the Executive shall receive severance equal to six months of the Executive’s then-current base salary, payable in accordance with the Company’s normal payroll practices, provided that the Executive timely executes and does not revoke a release of claims in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Company and continues to comply with the Executive’s obligations under this Agreement. No severance is payable in the event of a resignation, termination for Cause, or expiration of employment, except as required by applicable law. “Cause” shall mean the Executive’s material misconduct, material breach of this Agreement or written Company policy, willful failure to perform material duties after written notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure where curable, conviction of or plea to a felony, or fraud or dishonesty involving the Company.
edits.name: 3. SEVERANCE

edits.text: 4. NON-COMPETE. To the extent permitted by applicable law, for twelve months following the Executive’s departure, the Executive shall not, within the geographic markets in which the Executive materially performed services for the Company during the twelve months preceding departure, perform services substantially similar to those performed for the Company for a business that competes directly with a business line for which the Executive had material responsibility or about which the Executive received material confidential information. This restriction does not prohibit passive ownership of less than two percent of a publicly traded company. The Executive shall not, during that period, knowingly solicit for employment any Company employee with whom the Executive had material business contact during the twelve months preceding departure. The restrictions in this Section apply only to the extent enforceable under applicable law.
edits.name: 4. NON-COMPETE

receiver.message_back: Please provide Schedule A and the applicable incentive plan with the next draft, and revise severance to at least 12 months’ base salary plus target bonus, payable upon a without-Cause termination or resignation for Good Reason, with a release limited to customary claims and no forfeiture for immaterial or disputed breaches. We also request deletion of the non-compete; at minimum, any restriction should be limited to specific, demonstrably confidential competitive information and should not bar employment with a competitor.

drafter.private_reasoning: Accept a 12-month severance framework and Good Reason trigger to move the deal forward, while making payment conditional on a customary, narrowly scoped release. Remove the employment-based non-compete and preserve protection for confidential information through confidentiality and tailored employee non-solicitation language. Do not disclose the client's confidential authorization ceiling. The provided materials do not include Schedule A or the incentive plan, so do not invent their terms; identify them for separate completion and delivery.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Attached is our revised draft. We have revised severance to provide 12 months of base salary plus target bonus following a termination without Cause or resignation for Good Reason, subject to a customary release limited to employment-related claims. We have also removed the restriction on working for a competitor and retained tailored protections for confidential information and employee relationships. Schedule A and the applicable incentive plan were not included in the materials available for this draft; we will provide them separately once the applicable salary and plan materials are confirmed.

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive the annual base salary set out in Schedule A, payable in accordance with the Company’s normal payroll practices and subject to applicable withholdings. Any bonus or incentive compensation shall be governed by the applicable written plan, a copy of which shall be provided to the Executive, and its terms as in effect for the applicable performance period. No amendment to a written plan shall retroactively reduce an award earned for a completed performance period. The Executive shall be eligible to participate in employee benefit plans made generally available to similarly situated executives, subject to the terms of those plans.
edits.name: Compensation

edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause or the Executive resigns for Good Reason, the Executive shall receive severance equal to twelve months of the Executive’s then-current base salary, plus the Executive’s target annual bonus for the year of termination (or, if no target has been established for that year, the most recent annual target bonus), less applicable withholdings. The severance shall be paid in substantially equal installments in accordance with the Company’s normal payroll practices over the twelve-month period following termination, subject to applicable law and the Executive’s timely execution and non-revocation of a release of claims limited to customary claims arising from or relating to the Executive’s employment or its termination. The release shall not waive claims that cannot lawfully be waived, claims to enforce this Agreement, or rights to indemnification or under applicable directors’ and officers’ insurance. The release shall not require a release of claims arising after its execution. A breach of this Agreement shall not result in forfeiture of severance unless it is a material breach established by a final, non-appealable determination or admitted in writing by the Executive. “Good Reason” means, without the Executive’s written consent, a material reduction in the Executive’s base salary or target bonus opportunity, a material diminution in the Executive’s duties, authority, or responsibilities, or a required relocation of the Executive’s principal workplace by more than 50 miles; provided that the Executive gives written notice of the condition within 90 days after becoming aware of it, the Company fails to cure it within 30 days after receiving notice, and the Executive resigns within 30 days after the cure period expires. “Cause” shall mean the Executive’s material misconduct, material breach of this Agreement or written Company policy, willful failure to perform material duties after written notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure where curable, conviction of or plea to a felony, or fraud or dishonesty involving the Company.
edits.name: Severance

edits.text: 4. CONFIDENTIALITY AND EMPLOYEE NON-SOLICITATION. The Executive shall not use or disclose the Company’s confidential information except as necessary to perform duties for the Company or as authorized in writing by the Company, subject to applicable law. This obligation does not apply to information that becomes publicly available through no breach by the Executive, was lawfully known to the Executive without restriction before disclosure by the Company, or is independently developed without use of the Company’s confidential information. Nothing in this Agreement prohibits the Executive from accepting employment with, or providing services to, a business that competes with the Company, or from using general skills, knowledge, and experience. For twelve months following the Executive’s departure, the Executive shall not knowingly solicit for employment any Company employee with whom the Executive had material business contact during the twelve months preceding departure; general solicitations not specifically directed at such employees and hiring resulting from such solicitations shall not violate this provision. Nothing in this Section limits protected activity or disclosures permitted by applicable law.
edits.name: Confidentiality and employee non-solicitation
